entries.title: Gaussian directed ground-state path model in C0120
entries.statement: For n>=1, put iid standard Gaussian weights g_v on vertices v of the nonnegative integer quadrant. Let P_n be all paths of n vertices that begin at (0,0) and move one unit right or up at each step, with no fixed endpoint. Define M_n=max_{p in P_n} sum_{v in p}g_v. This is the zero-temperature 1+1-dimensional model of Chatterjee's Section 8, Theorem 8.1; that theorem bounds Var(M_n) by C n/log n for n>=2.
assumptions: path contains the origin and n-1 moves

entries.title: First Gaussian chaos and persistent polymer overlap (draft)
entries.statement: [DRAFT: author proof; independent w497 review pending.] In the Gaussian directed ground-state model with n-vertex free-endpoint up/right paths, let p_v=P(v belongs to the unique maximizing path), let M_n be its maximal path sum, and let D_n(1) be the squared L2 norm of the first-degree Gaussian Hermite projection of M_n-E M_n. Then D_n(1)=sum_v p_v^2>=H_n=sum_{j=1}^n 1/j. For the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck coupling g^t=e^{-t}g+sqrt(1-e^{-2t})g' with independent g', the expected overlap of maximizing paths tends to D_n(1) as t tends to infinity. This lower floor does not give the desired power upper bound on Var(M_n).
assumptions: exact model as defined by this bundle's model entry
Gaussian integration by parts for Lipschitz maxima

relations.rationale: The p_v layer normalization and unique maximizing path use the exact Gaussian quadrant/free-endpoint model, including the origin.
